project: WO-D2 — Reference Schemas for Batch Work, States, and Relations
description: Publish canonical packaged reference documentation that makes the FACTORY_REQUEST_BATCH shape, Work state lifecycle, and DEPENDS_ON, PARENT_CHILD, and SAME_NAME semantics implementation-ready for customers. The concrete change extends the established batch-inputs, work, relationships, and guard-linked topics so operators can author valid batches and predict joined-input dispatch, including batch-wide name uniqueness, same-batch-only relation endpoints, and the post-A1 rule that dependencies on every joined input gate dispatch.

context.customerAsk: Document the FACTORY_REQUEST_BATCH shape, Work states and transitions, and especially the difference between DEPENDS_ON, PARENT_CHILD, and SAME_NAME joining, including exactly what gates dispatch after the A1 fix. Capture the batch-wide unique-name and same-batch relation constraints discovered through live operator failures, publish the guidance through canonical docs/reference topics, execute every shown CLI invocation against the current binary, and verify packaged docs behavior with make docs-reference-smoke and make verify-fast.
context.problem: Operators currently have to infer critical submission and scheduling rules from scattered contract, guard, and runtime material. This caused rejected live submissions for duplicate names and relations outside the submitted batch, while incomplete documentation of SAME_NAME joins and dependency gating delayed diagnosis of dispatch-before-dependency behavior. Work-state names and lifecycle categories are also easy to conflate, so customers cannot reliably predict starting placement, progression, or completion semantics.
context.solution: Extend the canonical docs/reference batch-inputs, work, and relationships topics, with focused links to guards, rather than introducing a parallel schema topic family. Document the public batch fields and atomic constraints, the authored Work-state lifecycle, and a direct comparison of dependency, lineage, and name-join behavior. Include a worked multi-input timeline stating that every DEPENDS_ON relation on every selected join input must be satisfied before dispatch, and prove all displayed CLI commands against the current built binary with real output or behavioral assertions.

acceptanceCriteria: you docs batch-inputs gives a complete, internally consistent FACTORY_REQUEST_BATCH reference, including works[], workTypeName, batch-wide unique work names, atomic validation, and the requirement that every relation source and target name a Work item in the same submitted batch.

you docs work explains authored state names, the INITIAL, PROCESSING, TERMINAL, and FAILED lifecycle categories, initial or explicitly requested placement, workstation-driven transitions, and the observable distinction between successful terminal and failed Work.

you docs relationships clearly distinguishes DEPENDS_ON, PARENT_CHILD, and SAME_NAME; documents source/target direction; and states that dispatch waits for every DEPENDS_ON relation on every input selected for a join, including secondary SAME_NAME-joined inputs.

All new or changed examples use public customer vocabulary, live under docs/reference, keep root docs as routing material, stay within the D2 cut list, and avoid unrelated documentation or implementation cleanup.

Every CLI invocation shown in changed documentation is executed against the current built binary during implementation, with actual stdout/stderr pasted into the PR evidence or asserted in behavioral coverage; the named verification commands go test ./pkg/transports/cli/..., make docs-reference-smoke, and make verify-fast pass.
Typecheck and tests pass; no NEW lint violations relative to current main, and the gates green on main (backend-size, pkg-maint, pkg-file-count, pkg-structure, vet) stay green.

The implementation/review loop continues until required CI is terminal and passing, all blocking PR conversation feedback is explicitly addressed, merge conflicts and shared-file changes are reconciled, and the PR is actually merged.

userStories.title: Author a valid batch request
userStories.description: As a factory operator, I want one authoritative batch schema guide so I can submit multiple Work items without discovering naming, work-type, or relation-scope constraints through rejection.
acceptanceCriteria: The batch guide identifies the public request discriminator, request-level fields, works[] fields, and relations[] fields, and uses workTypeName rather than retired internal aliases.
The guide states that Work names must be unique across the entire batch and explains that relations resolve by those names.
The guide states that each relation's source and target must both name Work in the same submitted batch; relations cannot point to existing Work from an earlier or different submission.

userStories.title: Understand Work states and transitions
userStories.description: As a factory author or operator, I want the Work reference to explain state categories and transitions so I can predict where submitted Work starts, how it advances, and when it is considered successful or failed.
acceptanceCriteria: The Work reference distinguishes customer-authored state names from the lifecycle categories INITIAL, PROCESSING, TERMINAL, and FAILED, with the runtime meaning of each category.
The guide explains that omitted batch works[].state uses the Work type's initial state, while an explicit state must be a valid state on that Work type and intentionally changes starting placement.
The guide explains that the factory topology and workstation outcome routes define available transitions; it does not imply a universal fixed sequence of state names.
The guide explains observable completion semantics, including that TERMINAL represents successful completion, FAILED represents failed completion, and both stop ordinary non-terminal processing.
State guidance cross-links to the batch, factory configuration, workstation, and Work-observation references without duplicating their full contracts.

userStories.title: Predict relation and joined-input dispatch behavior
userStories.description: As a factory author, I want dependency, lineage, and name-join semantics compared directly so I can choose the correct construct and know exactly when a multi-input workstation may dispatch.
acceptanceCriteria: A comparison explains that DEPENDS_ON is a submitted batch relation for prerequisite-state gating, PARENT_CHILD is a submitted batch relation for parent lineage and parent-aware fan-in, and SAME_NAME is a per-input workstation guard that correlates inputs by authored Work name rather than a batch relation.

Direction is explicit: for DEPENDS_ON, the source is blocked by the target; for PARENT_CHILD, the source is the child and the target is the parent; for SAME_NAME, matchInput identifies the peer input whose selected Work name must equal the guarded input's Work name.
The guide states that SAME_NAME only selects compatible joined inputs and does not satisfy, replace, or create a dependency or parent lineage.

The dispatch invariant is explicit: after all join guards select a complete input binding, the scheduler evaluates every DEPENDS_ON relation on every selected input, and any missing target or target not in its requiredState prevents dispatch—including a dependency carried only by a secondary SAME_NAME-joined input.

A worked two-input example and timeline show that the workstation remains undispatched while the secondary joined input's prerequisite is incomplete and becomes eligible only after that prerequisite reaches the required state, subject to all other guards, capacity, and scheduler rules.
Every CLI invocation added or changed in this story is run against the current binary and its real output is pasted into PR evidence or asserted by behavioral coverage.
make docs-reference-smoke passes.
